subject: MerchantX: DPA path proposal & SCC module recommendation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@merchantx.com>, Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@merchantx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: MerchantX: DPA path proposal & SCC module recommendation

Hi Tom and Sarah,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on the integration pattern and the data flows you outlined. Per our discussion I wanted to put a concise proposal on the DPA/SCC path and the next steps we recommend so procurement and legal can move quickly.

Summary of what we heard:
- MerchantX will act as the controller for customer account data and transaction metadata; Redwood will process inference requests and store transient logs for 30 days (configurable).
- MerchantX requires an EU-compliant contract path (SCCs) and confirmation of SOC 2 Type II in-scope controls.
- No HIPAA required for the initial integration; you may revisit later for PII-heavy workflows.

Proposal (recommended path):
1) DPA request: we suggest the standard Redwood DPA with Controller/Processor clauses mirrored to reflect MerchantX as Controller, Redwood as Processor. Attached: MerchantX_DPA_Request_v1.docx (fillable).
2) SCC module: recommend the Module 2 (Processor to Controller) + Module 3 backup where needed; attached: Redwood_SCC_Module_Matrix.pdf (summary).
3) Evidence: Redwood will share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA (we're currently in rolling renewal; latest cert on file is 2026-06).
4) Questionnaire: to kick off security review, please complete the vendor security questionnaire link below — it helps us scope any compensating controls quickly. Link attached and pasted in the doc.

Immediate next steps we propose for this week:
- MerchantX procurement/legal: review the attached DPA draft and indicate if you need Redwood to sign MerchantX redlines or prefer to route via your standard procurement clause set. (action: MerchantX)
- MerchantX security: start the vendor questionnaire (link below). We'll review responses and provide SOC 2 evidence. (action: MerchantX)
- Redwood: if redlines are posted we’ll triage within 48 hours and suggest SCC module mapping back to you. (action: Redwood)

Attachments: MerchantX_DPA_Request_v1.docx (docx), Redwood_SCC_Module_Matrix.pdf (pdf)
Vendor questionnaire: https://forms.redwood.ai/vendor-questionnaire/MerchantX-4592

If helpful I can set a short 30-min follow-up with legal/security from both sides — propose Thursday 10/29 at 10am CET.

Thanks,

Ben Carter

Subject: Re: MerchantX: DPA path proposal & SCC module recommendation

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications before we loop legal:

1) Storage/retention: you mentioned 30 days by default. Can you confirm whether session logs that include masked PII are retained at all after 30 days or truncated earlier? We need to ensure we can represent that in the DPA.
2) SOC 2: please confirm the date of the most recent Type II report and whether redacted reports are possible (we will handle under NDA).
3) SCCs: Procurement prefers minimal modules. Can you explain why Module 3 would be needed as a backup?

Procurement is OK to review the DPA draft — they typically prefer to produce a redline rather than accept vendor language. We'll start that tonight.

Can we take the follow-up at 10am CET on 10/29 — that works for our security lead.

Tom
Head of Platform Integrations

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MerchantX: DPA path proposal & SCC module recommendation

Tom — great questions. Short answers below and I'll have Priyom pick up the detailed evidentiary notes.

1) Retention: default is 30 days for request logs. Session-level payloads containing masked PII are removed from searchable logs within 24 hours and full payloads are truncated/hashed at 30 days. We can include explicit language in the DPA to reflect the 24-hour masked payload truncation + 30-day log retention.

2) SOC 2: our most recent Type II audit report date is 2026-06-15. We can share a redacted PDF under NDA — I'll put the NDA link in the questionnaire and Priyom will coordinate delivery.

3) SCC modules: Module 2 covers the Processor-to-Controller flow you described. Module 3 becomes relevant when there is potential onward transfer to subprocessors located outside the EEA where Controller responsibilities need to be preserved — it's more of a fallback we propose so contracts don't stall if a subprocessor scenario appears in onboarding. If you prefer, we can provisionally present Module 2 only and add Module 3 in an appendix.

Follow-up: 10am CET today works — I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Ben
